title: C++20: from first program to reliable systems
summary: 42 planned lessons teach language fundamentals, ownership, portable builds, testing, concurrency and evidence-based performance. No compiler adapter is activated.
north_star: Build, test, explain and deliver a portable bounded C++20 program whose ownership, failure and performance claims survive independent review.

stages.title: Build a reliable mental model
stages.outcome: Predict small examples, perform bounded changes and independently verify the first capstone.

stages.title: Compose and debug real systems
stages.outcome: Combine the mechanisms with explicit ownership, tests, failure cases and repeatable delivery.

stages.title: Defend engineering decisions
stages.outcome: Reason about concurrency or distributed control, measure tradeoffs and present a reviewed recovery/release capstone.

lessons.title: Files, terminals and the compile-to-run journey
lessons.outcome: Distinguish source, compiler output and a running process without requiring another programming language.
lessons.lab: Trace a supplied hello.cpp, compiler transcript and exit-status worksheet; identify which file is editable.
lessons.verification: Label source/object/executable correctly and classify one compile error, one link error and one runtime failure.

lessons.title: Your first C++20 target
lessons.outcome: Build and run a small program through a named CMake target.
lessons.lab: Configure a clean out-of-source Debug build, compile hello and run it with fixed input.
lessons.verification: CTest passes and stdout is exactly hello, learner; rebuilding after one source edit changes only the intended output.

lessons.title: Values, types and conversions
lessons.outcome: Choose an integer or floating type and predict conversions before executing.
lessons.lab: Trace integer division, explicit conversion and a signed-versus-unsigned comparison over small fixtures.
lessons.verification: Explain 7/2 versus 7.0/2 and reject a negative count before conversion to an unsigned size.

lessons.title: Branches, loops and state traces
lessons.outcome: Write a bounded loop with an explicit invariant.
lessons.lab: Implement positive-value counting over empty, mixed and all-negative vectors using supplied loop scaffolding.
lessons.verification: Counts are 0, 3 and 0 for the published fixtures; no input is modified and each loop terminates.

lessons.title: Functions and parameter contracts
lessons.outcome: Separate input, output, precondition and postcondition in a function.
lessons.lab: Extract a unit-conversion function and compare value and reference parameters.
lessons.verification: Normal and boundary cases return the specified values; tests demonstrate which argument can change.

lessons.title: Strings and trustworthy integer input
lessons.outcome: Separate valid input from a failed parse without guessing from a numeric result.
lessons.lab: Parse whole integer tokens with from_chars and reject trailing characters, overflow and empty input.
lessons.verification: 42 succeeds; 42x, empty text and an out-of-range decimal are rejected with distinct recorded reasons.

lessons.title: Vectors and standard algorithms
lessons.outcome: Use an owning sequence and choose an algorithm with a clear order contract.
lessons.lab: Sort a copy, find a value and accumulate a supplied integer sequence.
lessons.verification: Original order is unchanged, sorted output is exact, and empty input has the specified identity result.

lessons.title: Copies, const references and lifetimes
lessons.outcome: Explain which object is owned and which name borrows it.
lessons.lab: Compare an independent vector copy with a const reference, then draw their lifetimes.
lessons.verification: A mutation changes the referenced original but not its copy; a returned reference to a local is rejected in review.

lessons.title: Vectors own; references borrow
lessons.outcome: Preserve ownership and perform checked access at collection boundaries.
lessons.lab: Complete the pilot's positive sum, replacement, checked read and filtered-copy contracts; diagnose an invalidated element reference.
lessons.verification: Fourteen explicit checks pass, including a 10000-element sum, negative indices and immutable input; explain why a dangling read must not be executed.

lessons.title: Structs, enums and meaningful states
lessons.outcome: Represent a record and distinguish valid states from arbitrary strings.
lessons.lab: Model a reading with an enum status and validate its construction boundary.
lessons.verification: Published valid records round-trip and malformed states cannot enter the accepted collection.

lessons.title: Files, streams and scoped resources
lessons.outcome: Read a text fixture while distinguishing EOF, parse failure and an I/O error.
lessons.lab: Load a small readings file with line numbers and deterministic error output.
lessons.verification: Missing file returns a nonzero status; final newline/no-final-newline fixtures yield the same records and all streams close on exit.

lessons.title: Headers, translation units and the linker
lessons.outcome: Distinguish a declaration from a definition and diagnose a link failure.
lessons.lab: Split a record parser into a header and implementation, then repair a missing definition fixture.
lessons.verification: A clean two-translation-unit build links once, and the negative fixture fails at the link phase rather than being misreported as a runtime failure.

lessons.title: Warnings and CTest as feedback
lessons.outcome: Turn behavioral contracts into tests that still run in Release builds.
lessons.lab: Add explicit failing-return checks and target-scoped warnings; repair a supplied conversion bug.
lessons.verification: CTest fails before the repair and passes afterward in Debug and Release; no correctness check depends on assert remaining enabled.

lessons.title: Capstone 1: auditable readings CLI
lessons.outcome: Deliver a deterministic small CLI from source and explain its failure behavior.
lessons.lab: Build a readings summarizer with clean input, malformed rows and an empty file.
lessons.verification: A fresh build passes normal/error fixtures, prints exact totals, returns documented statuses and preserves the input bytes.

lessons.title: RAII and unique ownership
lessons.outcome: Tie resource lifetime to an object and justify unique ownership.
lessons.lab: Wrap a fake handle with an observable close counter and use unique_ptr where dynamic lifetime is needed.
lessons.verification: Each acquired handle closes exactly once on normal return and exception paths; no raw owning new/delete is required.

lessons.title: Move semantics and the rule of zero
lessons.outcome: Choose copying, moving or borrowing from an ownership contract.
lessons.lab: Instrument a value type, then replace unnecessary manual special members with standard members.
lessons.verification: Behavioral tests remain exact and the learner states which moved-from guarantees are used instead of assuming an empty source.

lessons.title: Errors as values and exceptions
lessons.outcome: Select optional, variant or an exception according to the caller's information needs.
lessons.lab: Implement an error-bearing parse result and a boundary that translates exceptions to a CLI status.
lessons.verification: Valid data, expected invalid input and unexpected I/O failure follow three specified paths without losing context.

lessons.title: Views, iterators and invalidation
lessons.outcome: Use spans and string views without extending the lifetime of their storage.
lessons.lab: Review invalidation cases and build a safe view-based scan over stable owned storage.
lessons.verification: Tests match the owning implementation, and a lifetime diagram identifies vector reallocation and temporary-string hazards.

lessons.title: Ranges and deliberate algorithms
lessons.outcome: Separate a lazy view from a materialized result and preserve ordering contracts.
lessons.lab: Compose filter/transform views and materialize a deterministic result using a qualified C++20 subset.
lessons.verification: Expected records match a simple reference loop; the view never outlives its owner and single-pass assumptions are identified.

lessons.title: Templates and concepts
lessons.outcome: Express a useful generic contract and read a constraint diagnostic.
lessons.lab: Write a constrained aggregation function and compile a deliberately unsupported call in a negative fixture.
lessons.verification: Valid integral and floating calls pass; an invalid type fails at the intended constraint with the documented diagnostic category.

lessons.title: Strong types and generic value APIs
lessons.outcome: Prevent mixing semantically different values with the same representation.
lessons.lab: Model identifiers and quantities as distinct value types with explicit operations.
lessons.verification: An invalid unit/identifier mix is rejected at compile time; equality and ordering obey the published laws.

lessons.title: Portable files and serialization
lessons.outcome: Define a durable wire format rather than dumping object memory.
lessons.lab: Encode a tiny versioned record with fixed widths, explicit byte order and length bounds.
lessons.verification: A published byte fixture decodes exactly; truncated, oversized and unknown-version records fail without out-of-bounds access.

lessons.title: Library boundaries and ABI
lessons.outcome: Separate source compatibility from binary compatibility.
lessons.lab: Export a small library with public/private headers and an explicit C-compatible boundary example.
lessons.verification: A separate consumer compiles against the public target; the learner identifies why a foreign STL object is not a portable C ABI.

lessons.title: Property tests and bounded fuzzing
lessons.outcome: Test invariants across more than hand-picked examples while preserving a reproducible failure.
lessons.lab: Run a deterministic generated corpus and, where the qualified profile supports it, a time-bounded libFuzzer job.
lessons.verification: A minimized bad fixture is retained, its seed/corpus hash reproduces it, and no fuzzer is reported passed when the tool is unavailable.

lessons.title: Sanitizers and observable memory failures
lessons.outcome: Use diagnostic builds to distinguish a memory error from a successful test run.
lessons.lab: Run curated lifetime/overflow negative fixtures under supported ASan/UBSan builds and fix the source.
lessons.verification: Positive fixtures pass; each negative fixture exits nonzero with the expected error class and symbolized source location; supported tools are recorded.

lessons.title: Debugging and measurement tools
lessons.outcome: Form a hypothesis from a stack, breakpoint or profile before editing code.
lessons.lab: Use a supplied crash and hot-loop fixture with the profile's available debugger and profiler.
lessons.verification: The selected frame/variable explains the failure, and an independent test distinguishes the proposed fix from the original behavior.

lessons.title: Reproducible dependencies and delivery
lessons.outcome: Build offline from reviewed inputs and name license/version obligations.
lessons.lab: Consume a pre-vendored tiny dependency through target-based CMake without configure-time downloads.
lessons.verification: Disconnected configure/build/CTest succeed; dependency versions and hashes are recorded and a missing fixture fails explicitly.

lessons.title: Capstone 2: reusable record library
lessons.outcome: Ship an installable library with robust parsing and an independent consumer.
lessons.lab: Deliver a versioned record library, corpus, package configuration and a relocation test.
lessons.verification: A clean consumer build and all corpus/property/sanitizer checks pass; no source-tree absolute path is required after installation.

lessons.title: Threads, joining and cancellation
lessons.outcome: Make thread lifetime and cancellation ownership explicit.
lessons.lab: Build a bounded task pair using jthread/stop_token when feature probes pass, with a documented joining alternative.
lessons.verification: Every worker terminates before its owner; cancellation reaches the intended checkpoint and no unsupported native library feature is silently assumed.

lessons.title: Mutexes, conditions and producer-consumer flow
lessons.outcome: Protect an invariant and use a predicate while waiting.
lessons.lab: Implement a bounded queue with condition_variable and deterministic close semantics.
lessons.verification: No item is lost or duplicated, queue capacity is never exceeded, and waiting threads exit after close without busy spinning.

lessons.title: Atomics and the memory model
lessons.outcome: Separate atomicity, ordering and visibility in an argument about a concurrent program.
lessons.lab: Analyze published litmus cases and implement a small acquire/release handoff.
lessons.verification: The happens-before argument names each synchronization edge; passing stress tests is not offered as proof of every allowed execution.

lessons.title: Bounded parallel work and failure propagation
lessons.outcome: Bound concurrency and transfer failures without abandoning owned work.
lessons.lab: Create a fixed-size executor with a bounded queue, cancellation and a failing task fixture.
lessons.verification: At most the configured worker count runs; a task failure is reported, all workers join and queued jobs follow the documented cancellation policy.

lessons.title: Testing concurrent code
lessons.outcome: Use deterministic scheduling evidence and separate race diagnostics from timing luck.
lessons.lab: Run controlled interleavings, stress fixtures and a separate TSan build where supported.
lessons.verification: Exact item-accounting checks pass and the curated race fixture is detected by TSan; no ASan/TSan combination is used.

lessons.title: Data layout, allocation and locality
lessons.outcome: Explain a measured cost using layout and allocation evidence.
lessons.lab: Compare equivalent array-of-struct and struct-of-array scans on fixed datasets.
lessons.verification: Results are identical; allocation counts and repeated timing distributions are reported with hardware/compiler/build metadata.

lessons.title: Algorithmic and representation choices
lessons.outcome: Choose an optimization from growth behavior and measured constraints.
lessons.lab: Compare two lookup strategies across fixed input sizes and adversarial duplicates.
lessons.verification: Correctness matches a reference implementation and measured operation counts explain the crossover without a universal speed claim.

lessons.title: Compile-time computation with a budget
lessons.outcome: Choose runtime or compile-time work according to observable cost and constraints.
lessons.lab: Build a constexpr lookup table and contrast a bounded consteval validation step.
lessons.verification: Runtime output matches its reference, invalid constant input fails compilation, and compile time remains within the declared job budget.

lessons.title: Composing generic interfaces
lessons.outcome: Balance reusable templates with comprehensible ownership and diagnostics.
lessons.lab: Design a constrained range pipeline with an explicitly owned result boundary.
lessons.verification: Several valid container inputs pass; an invalid borrow is rejected in review and an unsupported type produces the intended constraint failure.

lessons.title: Numerical and integer correctness
lessons.outcome: State a numeric error/overflow contract instead of assuming one machine result.
lessons.lab: Compare exact integer accumulation and floating algorithms on cancellation and large-magnitude fixtures.
lessons.verification: Integer overflow is prevented, not relied upon; floating results satisfy justified absolute/relative tolerances and a failure counterexample is explained.

lessons.title: C interfaces and loading boundaries
lessons.outcome: Define ownership and error transport across a language/binary boundary.
lessons.lab: Expose a small C ABI with paired acquire/release operations using only reviewed fixture libraries.
lessons.verification: An independent consumer observes the same contract, each handle is released once and no arbitrary host library path is accepted.

lessons.title: Hardening parsers and execution boundaries
lessons.outcome: Treat input lengths, paths and external effects as part of correctness.
lessons.lab: Attack a supplied parser with oversized lengths and traversal strings inside the isolated fixture workspace.
lessons.verification: Rejected inputs produce bounded errors, no write escapes the fixture output root and process/output/time limits are tested rather than assumed.

lessons.title: Portable release and performance evidence
lessons.outcome: Publish a source release with precise platform and performance claims.
lessons.lab: Produce reproducible CMake presets, offline inputs, correctness checks and per-platform evidence records.
lessons.verification: Clean builds pass on each claimed target; unsupported sanitizer/toolchain cells stay marked pending and timing data includes uncertainty.

lessons.title: Capstone 3: bounded parallel analyzer
lessons.outcome: Deliver a correct concurrent analyzer and defend its lifetime, failure and performance decisions.
lessons.lab: Build a fixed-memory record analyzer with cancellation, malformed-input handling and an independent consumer.
lessons.verification: Reference output, cancellation/failure cleanup, sanitizer profiles and repeated benchmarks pass; no throughput gain is claimed without comparable evidence.

capstones.title: Auditable readings CLI
capstones.brief: cpp-014 combines parsing, files, meaningful records and testable CLI behavior.
deliverables: CMake project and clean source tree
CTest transcript and one-page failure contract
acceptance: Fresh Debug and Release builds pass exact output/status checks.
Malformed input is identified by line and does not partially overwrite input.
The learner explains a copy, a borrow and a scoped resource without opening the solution.

capstones.title: Reusable record library
capstones.brief: cpp-028 produces a versioned installable library and an independent consumer.
deliverables: Public/private target boundary and package configuration
Versioned byte fixtures and generated/fuzz corpus
Supported sanitizer evidence and relocated consumer build
acceptance: A consumer builds without source-tree absolute paths.
Malformed/truncated/oversized fixtures fail without memory errors.
Supported diagnostic profiles pass; unavailable native profiles are explicitly pending.

capstones.title: Bounded parallel analyzer
capstones.brief: cpp-042 integrates ownership, concurrent flow, failure propagation and defensible measurement.
deliverables: Bounded worker/queue implementation and cancellation contract
Reference results, malformed-input corpus and resource ledger
Repeated benchmark distributions and portability review
acceptance: No item is lost/duplicated and output matches the reference for every fixture.
Task failure/cancellation join all workers and preserve completed evidence.
Performance comparisons preserve semantics and record uncertainty, architecture and build flags.

concept.title: Owning values and borrowed access
concept.explanation: A vector owns its elements. Copying it creates independent values; a reference borrows an existing object and does not extend arbitrary element lifetimes. at() checks a boundary and reports out_of_range instead of allowing an unchecked access.
concept.worked_example: Copy {4,7,9}, change original.at(0) to 5, then observe copy=4 original=5. Access at(original.size()) must throw std::out_of_range and print bounds rejected.

prediction.prompt: values is {3,8}; snapshot is a copy, alias is a const reference to values, then values.at(0)=4. What are snapshot.at(0) and alias.at(0)?
choices: 3 and 4: the copy is independent and the alias sees the original.
4 and 4: all vector assignments share storage.
3 and 3: const prevents any name from changing the original.
prediction.explanation: const restricts mutation through alias; it does not freeze the original through other valid names. The vector copy owns separate elements.

hint_steps: Draw two owning vector boxes and one arrow before changing any code.
Check a signed index before converting it to a vector size; test empty input and index==size.
Keep an owned value or reacquire an element after a growth operation; never use a possibly invalidated reference to discover whether it dangles.
pilot.transfer_prompt: Apply the same ownership/boundary reasoning to a filtered temperature batch whose output must survive later mutation of its input.
rubric: Predict copy/reference behavior correctly before execution.
Pass14normal/boundary checks without mutating read-only inputs.
Explain an invalidated-element lifetime and two safe repair strategies.
Use CMake/CTest with explicit nonzero failures, including Release.
State which platform/compiler/sanitizer claims remain unverified.
